text.p: Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA40
Cocoa futures look set to re-test support after a corrective move higher last week, analysts said.
Traders called benchmark September cocoa to open some two to three sterling lower.

September reached a high of 1,063 stg a tonne on Friday, but ended lower. "I see the whole move up to 1,063 as corrective," said Adrian Haylor, technical analyst at Sucden, noting Friday's reversal to the downside.
Friday's high was likely to be the full extent of the correction, Haylor said. "I think the market will come off and probably re-test 1,000."
If cocoa were to move higher, there would be further resistance above the 1,063 high at 1,070 and then at the gap between 1,087 and 1,108, he said. "I don't think it's likely to be filled."

"The strength of sterling was largely to blame for the sell-off in London on Friday," brokers GNI said. "However, the fact that New York fell as well and ended on a weak note signals the negative tone of the market at present." GNI said there was "room for the market to take another big leg down."
New York cocoa futures ended sharply lower and towards the bottom of the day's range in light trading on Friday, pressured by local and speculative selling, traders said.
